items.description: Laptop replacement - equivalent to the damaged model (repair uneconomic per supplier report)
items.rationale: Policy 2.6 and 7.1.10: Sudden accidental damage to portable equipment is covered, and the battery health waiver means the laptop is not excluded despite battery <80%. Indemnity is capped at the cost of an equivalent replacement, not a higher-spec model. Reference Case 22 (laptop repair t < 313) and market for mid/high-end laptops suggest a moderate threshold.

items.description: Higher-spec upgrade difference (better model than the one damaged)
items.rationale: Policy 7.1.9: No betterment over pre-loss standard; indemnity is limited to equivalent replacement, not upgrades. Reference cases confirm upgrades are not indemnified.

items.description: Tablet screen repair (struck in the same bag)
items.rationale: Policy 2.6 and 7.1.10: Sudden accidental damage to portable equipment is covered. The tablet was in the same incident and shows impact damage. Reference Case 22 (screen repair t < 313) and typical tablet screen repair costs suggest a moderate threshold.
Policy 5.2.3: Diagnostic costs for damaged portable equipment are covered up to EUR 250 per event. Both devices were affected in the same event, so a single capped threshold applies.

items.description: New laptop carry bag (not damaged in the incident)
items.rationale: Policy 7.1.5 and 7.1.8: Only items damaged by the insured event are covered. The bag was not damaged, so this is not indemnified.

items.description: Extended warranty on the replacement laptop
items.rationale: Policy 3.5(f) and 7.1.8(e): Extended warranties and future service contracts are expressly excluded from cover.

items.description: Data recovery from the damaged laptop drive
items.rationale: Policy 3.5(d) and 4.3(c): Data recovery and restoration are excluded unless specifically endorsed, which is not the case here.
Policy 3.5(d) and 4.3(c): Administration fees for data recovery are excluded for the same reason as above.
